_: Hand-resolved v83->v84 sites that no automatic tier can reach, plus source-bug findings. Every entry states the evidence that was checked against the two v84 dumps. resolve.py applies these last; verify.py re-checks them like any other patch.

_0x00780743_NOT_SHIPPED.why_not_shipped: Key is prefixed so resolve.py does NOT apply it. The ADDRESS is high-confidence, but the site fails the SHAPE gate for a real reason: v83 is `mov dword ptr [ebp+8], imm32` and v84 is `mov dword ptr [ebp-0x3c4], imm32`. Same mnemonic and same operand roles, different displacement width -- so same_shape() rejects it and the resolver reports a false positive. That gate is the thing keeping this table trustworthy, and overriding it on one agent's call, for a feature that is a NO-OP at the default config (v84 already holds 140 here), is a bad trade. Ship it only after same_shape() learns that disp8 and disp32 forms of the same instruction are the same shape -- a general fix that would need the whole 327-row table re-verified, since it can flip other verdicts. Until then speedMovementCap is 2 of 3 sites: raising it above 140 may still be clamped by whatever path this site governs.
_0x00780743_NOT_SHIPPED.evidence: speedMovementCap, 1 of 3. v83 `c7 45 08 d1 2f 01 00` mov [ebp+8],0x12fd1. Byte signatures are useless here: 0 of 119 masked 24-byte windows spanning the whole v83 function 0x0077F4C9-0x007807BF occur anywhere in v84, because v84 recompiled it (sub esp,0x3f0 vs v83's 0x28). Resolved through the call graph instead: v83 0x0077F4C9 has exactly two callers, 0x00A085BA and 0x00A22772; both locate uniquely in BOTH dumps (-> 0x00A52890, 0x00A6DC72) and following the same call index in each lands independently on v84 0x007A2161. Inside it the block 0x007A45EC-0x007A4678 matches v83 0x0078072E-0x0078076A instruction for instruction with every struct offset preserved (+0x158, +0x150, 0x64). 0x007A4622 is the only imm32==0x8c write-to-local in the function; its +-16B masked context is unique across v84 .text in both dumps. Delta +0x23EDF sits between resolved neighbours 0x00776B5F (+0x22967) and 0x007B2C97 (+0x25D47).
_0x00780743_NOT_SHIPPED.caveat: off_v84 is 6, NOT the source's 3. v83 uses a disp8 ([ebp+8]) so its imm32 starts at +3; v84's larger frame needs a disp32 ([ebp-0x3c4]), making the instruction 10 bytes with the imm32 at +6. Writing at +3 on v84 would overwrite the top three displacement bytes plus the low byte of the immediate -- stack corruption, not a cap change.

0x008D1F65.evidence: AdjustStatusBarBG. Four independent lines, all checked in both dumps. (1) MEMBER: v83 reads the object through `add eax,0xCCC` at 0x008D1F46; v84 through `lea ecx,[esi+0xD04]` at 0x00906D3C. 0xCCC+0x38=0xD04, and +0x38 is the measured shift for every CUIStatusBar member above ~0xC40 (v83 0xCD0->v84 0xD08 and 0xCD4->0xD0C are the two confirmed cave sites; the 0xCD4 group is 11 sites in v83 and 11 in v84 in the same order). (2) SEH ALIGNMENT: the `mov [ebp-4],state` unwind markers run 0x72,0x73,0x74,0x73,0x75,0x76,0x75,0x77,0x78,0x77,0x79,0x7A,0x7B in v83 and 0x7E,0x7F,0x80,0x7F,0x81,0x82,0x81,0x83,0x84,0x83,0x85,0x86,0x87 in v84 -- a constant +0xC with NO insertion or deletion across the whole 0x008D1E7B..0x008D2185 / 0x00906CE5..0x00906EC7 span. The anchor at the far end of that run is P248 0x008D217C->0x00906EBE, already verified independently. 0x008D1F65 and 0x00906D39 sit in the corresponding sub-block (v83 0x73/0x74, v84 0x7F/0x80). (3) PREAMBLE: both blocks construct the same pair of ZXString temporaries into [ebp-0x28] and [ebp-0x50]/[ebp-0x4c] with the same `push ebx ; lea ecx ; call <ctor>` twice, and both are followed by `mov ecx,eax ; call`. (4) ARGUMENT POSITION: 0x16 is the same argument in the same position in both. Ordinally it is also the 2nd of 3 `push 0x16` in each image's status-bar region, which is how phase 1 guessed it -- that alone was NOT sufficient evidence, because the 2nd v84 site has the shape of the *Input* cave, not the BG cave.
0x008D1F65.cave_body_v84: push nStatusBarY ; push edi ; lea ecx,[esi+0x0D04] ; jmp [dwStatusBarBackgroundPosRetn]
0x008D1F65.caveat: REDESIGNED CAVE, NOT A RE-POINT. v84 recompiled the call: v83 was a vtable call `call [ecx+0x90]` taking both ZXStrings BY VALUE (4x movsd each), v84 is a direct thiscall `call 0x428CEF` with `this = esi+0xD04` taking them BY POINTER. So the v83 displaced run (`push 0x16 ; movsd ; push 0` = 5 bytes) does not exist in v84. The v84 run is `push 0x16 ; push edi ; lea ecx,[esi+0xD04]` = 2+1+6 = 9 bytes, which is the SAME shape as AdjustStatusBarInput. Cave size is therefore 9 (5-byte jmp + 4 nops), retn 0x00906D42. Phase 1's note proposed `nops 3` -- that is arithmetically impossible, a 5-byte E9 does not fit in 3 bytes, and 3 was the only other whole-instruction tiling at this address. UNPROVEN: that 0x16 still drives the background layer's Y in v84's UI.wz. The address, the tiling and the body are proven at the binary; the visual effect is not.

0x00522C73.evidence:
block 1 (guild invite). v84 vanilla Y 0x1EC, not 0x1FC.
GROUP I JOIN. The eleven pop-up blocks are near-identical, so no context signature can separate them once v84's two changed immediates are wildcarded (measured: masking both makes the +-32B window match 3 v83 sites and 7 v84 sites). The join is therefore ORDINAL, and it is forced by four independent constraints that all agree:
(a) UNIQUE MARKERS. Five blocks carry a marker that occurs exactly once per image: delay literal 0x7530 (v83 0x00523595 / v84 0x0052F18C), delay 0x1770 (0x00523BB1 / 0x0052F7F3), a `neg esi ; sbb esi,esi` head (0x00523DA5 / 0x0052F9E7), head immediate 0x1F2 with a `sub` (0x0052418C / 0x0052FDCE), and the sid-less `push 0` variant (0x0052307E / 0x0052E84C). ALL FIVE were already resolved independently by T1/T2 in phase 1 and every one lands exactly where the ordinal join puts it.
(b) DIALOG ID. Each block ends `lea eax,[ebp+0xc] ; push <sid>`. v84 shifted the string table by exactly +2: 0x50F->0x511, 0x510->0x512, 0x512->0x514. Every mapped pair obeys it. The two v84 blocks that do NOT (0x0052EB3F sid 0x159A and 0x0052EF50 sid 0x1599) are dialogs v84 ADDED -- excluding them makes the counts exactly 12 = 12.
(c) GAP SEQUENCE. Consecutive head-to-head gaps agree exactly over runs: v83 +0x1F4,+0x1FE,+0x1E9 == v84 +0x1F4,+0x1FE,+0x1E9 across the last four blocks, and v83 +0x1F2 == v84 +0x1F2 across blocks 6-7.
(d) MONOTONICITY. The twelve deltas are non-decreasing: 0xB7AC, 0xB7BE, 0xB7CE, 0xB9F3, 0xBBF7, 0xBC09, 0xBC09, 0xBC42, 0xBC42, 0xBC42, 0xBC42, 0xBC54 -- consistent with v84 only inserting code, and P042 (0x00523154->0x0052E931, delta 0xB7DD) falls in its correct slot between blocks 3 and 4. Injectivity holds: 12 distinct -> 12 distinct.
Phase 1's conclusion that v84 'restructured' this group was wrong. Eleven of the twelve blocks are byte-identical to v83 apart from two immediates and the relocated call targets. The reason every tier missed them is that v84 changed BOTH patched immediates (0x1FC->0x1EC and 0x1D0->0x19D) on the majority, and T1b masks only the site's own.

0x0052307E.evidence:
block 3 (trade). THE ONE BLOCK v84 GENUINELY RESTRUCTURED. v83 `mov eax,0x1FC ; sub eax,ecx`; v84 `mov ecx,0x1FC ; sub ecx,eax` -- registers swapped, so SHAPE fails and operand geometry (imm32 at +1) is the correct test; regalloc is set. v84 then ADDS `test esi,esi ; jne ; mov ecx,0x1EC ; add edx,-0x33`, i.e. a second variant of the same dialog selected at runtime on the same esi the sid idiom tests. Identity is certain: both blocks end with the identical computed-sid idiom `neg esi ; sbb esi,esi ; and esi,0xF19 ; add esi,0x50F` -> `and esi,0xF1A ; add esi,0x511`, and both carry the `push 0 ; push 0xFF ; push 0` tail that no other block in either image has. UNPATCHED SECOND ARM: 0x0052E85C (`mov ecx,0x1EC`) and the `add edx,-0x33` at 0x0052E861 have NO v83 counterpart. If the esi!=0 path is ever taken that variant stays at its vanilla position. Patching it needs a value nobody can derive offline.

0x0060D85B.why_not_portable:
The cave displaces 51 bytes of v83 argument setup and replays it with four constants rewritten. v84 recompiled that setup: the baked-in literal coordinates were hoisted into stack locals ([ebp-0x18], [ebp-0x1c], [ebp-0x24], [ebp-0x14], [ebp+8]) and a SECOND ARM was added, selected by `cmp ebx,4 ; jne` at 0x00622907, with its own constants (0x13B, 0xA9, 0x29, -0x82) that have no v83 counterpart. The 51-byte sequence the cave replays does not exist in v84 -- `and edx,0x3f ; add edx,0x21` (6 bytes) does not occur ANYWHERE in the v84 image, at any address.
The cave has four effects (myWidth = W-800, myHeight = H-600):
  1. add edx, a2y   where a2y = H-600      -- the Y coordinate
  2. and ebx, a3    where a3 = 25          -- replaces the literal 0x64
  3. add eax, a1x   where a1x = W-800      -- replaces `xor eax,eax`
  4. mov eax, a2x   where a2x = W-949      -- replaces the literal -149
(a1y = -250 is assigned in Client.cpp:561 and never read by the body -- dead.)
TWO of the four map onto plain immediate writes in v84, and both are exact:
  effect 2 -> 0x00622956 + 2   `and ebx,0x64` (83 E3 64), imm8, write 25
  effect 4 -> 0x00622911 + 3   `mov [ebp-0x1c],0xFFFFFF6B`, imm32, write W-949
TWO do not:
  effect 1: v84's Y is `dec eax ; and eax,0x3f ; add eax,0x21` at 0x00622900-06. The add is `83 C0 21`, a SIGN-EXTENDED imm8, so 0x21 + (H-600) overflows it at any height above 706. It needs a cave of its own or a widened instruction.
  effect 3: v84 has no `xor eax,eax` in the argument block at all -- that argument is now `push [ebp-0x24]`, which holds the computed coordinate in arm 1 and edi in arm 2. There is no single immediate that corresponds.
And nothing offline can say what the SECOND ARM's four constants should become.
0x0060D85B.decision: NOT SHIPPED, deliberately. Applying the two portable effects without the other two would put the descriptor at a position neither v83-correct nor v84-correct, which is worse than leaving it at v84's own. The two addresses above are recorded so whoever finishes this has them, but the remaining work needs a running client to see the widget -- it is a design job, not an address-translation job.
0x0060D85B.cost_if_left: World-select descriptor stays at its v84 position while the rest of the login screen moves. Step 2 of the manual procedure in README.md covers it.
0x0060D85B.confidence: function resolved: high. cave portability: NOT PORTABLE, proven at the binary. correct v84 replacement: UNPROVEN, needs a launch.
0x0060D85B.note_2026_08_18: resolving P126 as an additive descriptor offset was a mismeasurement for the wrong control; the channel-select CLICK issue is a separate control (0x2ac-byte cell structs, hit-test near 0x0060cd22) and will be fixed there, not here.

P113.fault: NOT A RESOLUTION CONSTANT. The site is `push 0x10 ; push 0x258 ; call 0x403196 ; pop ecx ; pop ecx ; mov [edi],eax` -- a two-argument cdecl allocator returning a pointer. The 600 is a sizeof, and Ezorsia matched it purely because the literal happens to be 600.
P113.proof: v84's counterpart is 0x005F8BCF, delta 0x14C2F, inside the monotone band [0x10789, 0x14E98] and the only `push 0x10 ; push <~600> ; call 0x403196` in it. v84 raised the literal to 0x260 = 608, while EVERY genuine resolution site in the set still reads 600. A structure grew by 8 bytes; a screen did not.
P113.fix: DO NOT PORT. Writing m_nGameHeight (720) there over-allocates by 112 bytes and is merely wasteful at 1280x720, but at any height below 608 it under-allocates and corrupts the heap. Dropped from the shipping set.

P031.fault: The instruction at 0x004D59B2 is `cmp ecx, 0x258` (81 F9 58 02 00 00) -- a 6-byte form whose imm32 starts at +2, not +1. The comment (`mov eax,800`) describes the neighbouring 0x004D599D, not this site.
P031.as_shipped: writes the 4 value bytes over 81 [F9 58 02 00], leaving 81 D0 02 00 00 00 = `adc eax, 2`, then a stray `add byte ptr [esi+0xE], bh`. Register and memory corruption, not a crash, which is why it survived.
P031.fix: offset 2, value m_nGameHeight (the operand really is the 600 height compare)

P311.fault: The instruction is `add eax, 0xFFFFFED4` (05 D4 FE FF FF) -- imm32 at +1, not +2. It is an `add`, not a `push`; the comment is wrong too.
P311.as_shipped: writes one byte past the immediate, corrupting the following `cmp dword ptr [esi+0x28], eax`.

P158.fault: 0x0064061D is `idiv ecx` (F7 F9) -- two bytes, no immediate at all. The `mov ecx, 0x258` the comment means is at 0x00640618, which the previous source line already patches.
P158.as_shipped: overwrites F7 [F9 8B 45 E0] -> F7 D0 02 00 00 = `not eax` plus garbage, directly on the divisor setup.
P158.fix: DELETE. 0x00640618+1 already applies the intended height. Do not port this operation.

P302_P304.source: Memory::WriteInt(0x009F7079, m_nGameHeight) // dd 600   AND   Memory::WriteInt(0x009F7078 + 1, m_nGameHeight)
P302_P304.fault: Not destructive, but redundant: 0x009F7078 is `push 0x258` so its imm32 IS 0x009F7079. The source writes the same two dwords twice under two spellings (lines 290/291 and 311/312).
P302_P304.fix: keep one spelling (0x009F7078 + 1 / 0x009F707D + 1); drop the other so the patch set has one row per real operand.

manifest_fill.fault: count is computed from the v83 literal length. v84's literal is one byte longer -- see the 0x00C08459 site entry above.

elevation_noop.fault: Intent is HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE (0x80000002) -> HKEY_CURRENT_USER (0x80000001) on a `push imm32`. In localhome.exe the push already reads 0x80000001, so the write is a no-op there. Not a bug in the source, but it means these three cannot be validated against this v83 reference.
elevation_noop.fix: no change; group A, already covered by edits\bypass.

ip_fill.fault: cosmetic: the count expression subtracts two 0x006Fxxxx addresses while the target is 0x00AFxxxx. The difference (0x2E) is what is used, so behaviour is correct, but the expression is a copy-paste artefact.
